title: Mg2Al–CO3 Layered Double Hydroxide for Pb(II) Removal from Water: Sorption Behavior and the Effect of AlIII→FeIII and MgII→ZnII Substitution in the Hydroxide Layer
content: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are attractive low-cost sorbents for lead-bearing effluents, but the way the chemical identity of the layer cations governs their capacity is difficult to establish because published values are obtained under different experimental conditions. In this work a carbonate-intercalated Mg2Al–CO3 phase was prepared by coprecipitation at constant pH and characterized by XRD, SEM–EDX, N2 sorption, DSC and pHPZC measurements; its Pb(II) sorption behavior was then examined as a function of sorbent dose, initial pH, contact time, initial concentration and temperature. Equilibrium was reached within 60 min, the pseudo-first-order equation described the kinetics (R2 = 0.9999), and the Redlich–Peterson and Langmuir models fitted the isotherms best, with a monolayer capacity of 59.1 mg g−1. The process was spontaneous and endothermic (ΔH° = 11.07 kJ mol−1), and the low sorption and activation energies (< 2 kJ mol−1) point to a predominantly physical, electrostatically driven uptake. These results were then compared with those we previously published for two isostructural phases obtained and tested under strictly identical conditions, Mg2[FeAl]–CO3 and Zn2[FeAl]–CO3. Partial replacement of AlIII by FeIII doubled the monolayer capacity, from 59.1 to 118.8 mg g−1, whereas replacing MgII by ZnII raised it to only 87.9 mg g−1. In both cases the gain tracked the increase in specific surface area and the loss of crystallinity, which identifies structural disorder rather than structural perfection as the parameter to optimize.
